They held office side by side: in 1995-96 Darlene chaired Student Affairs while Carlene chaired Legislative Research, and in 1996-97 Carlene was Vice President while Darlene was Secretary. A name-similarity sweep flags them every time; they must not be merged and neither may wear the other's face. Confirmed independently against the university's own records on 1 September 2026. name: 1989 Talisman, printed pages 352-353
detail: One leaf is missing from the TopSCHOLAR scan of the 1989 Talisman. PDF leaf 178 ends on printed page 351 and leaf 179 opens on printed page 354, so the index runs A to Crawford and then jumps to Foe. The whole D and E section of the index, and the first half of F, is simply not in the file. That is why Bill Engle cannot be looked up in the volume that covers his first year. Every leaf after 178 is therefore one printed spread further on than the arithmetic suggests: pages are 2*leaf-6 up to leaf 178 and 2*leaf-4 after it.

name: TopSCHOLAR Talismans 1982-1991
detail: Every volume of this run is scanned at about 96 dpi, roughly 816 by 1123 pixels per printed page, except the 1983 volume which is 1892 by 2386 and has no OCR text layer at all. At that ceiling a class portrait cell comes out between 70 and 160 pixels wide, which is small but real, while a face in a club or Associated Student Government group photograph comes out at 40 to 60 pixels, which is not usable for anything. Plan on the class portrait grids and treat the group photographs as name lists, not as picture sources. Volume record numbers run 405 for 1982, 406 and 407 for the two parts of 1983, then 408 to 415 for 1984 through 1991. Leaf to printed page: 1982 page = leaf-3; 1983 part 2 page = leaf+193; 1984 and 1991 page = 2*leaf-6; 1985 page = 2*leaf-4; 1988 and 1990 page = leaf-3; 1989 see the entry above.

name: Debby Clark

topic: TopSCHOLAR access, settled 4 September 2026
note: Record pages on digitalcommons.wku.edu serve 200 to a plain script. The file endpoint /cgi/viewcontent.cgi does NOT: it still returns 403 to curl while the human's own browser gets 200 on the same URL, because the block is on the TLS fingerprint and no header or cookie reproduces it. An agent reported the block lifted after seeing a record page succeed; it had not. Reading catalogue metadata is fine from a script. Downloading a scanned volume is not, and scripts/browser_bridge.py exists for that.

topic: THE WAYBACK ROUTE INTO TOPSCHOLAR, found 4 September 2026
note: TopSCHOLAR's file endpoint /cgi/viewcontent.cgi refuses every script and even headless Chrome with a 403; the block is on the TLS fingerprint. The Internet Archive has mirrored those same PDFs and serves them to plain curl. Fetching http://web.archive.org/web/2024id_/https://digitalcommons.wku.edu/cgi/viewcontent.cgi?article=<N>&context=dlsc_ua_records returned a real 4.6 MB Herald issue on the first try. Get <N> from the record page, which curl CAN read with -L: it carries the viewcontent link. The `id_` in the wayback path matters, it asks for the raw file rather than the archive's HTML wrapper. USE curl -L. Without it the Wayback URL returns a bare 302 and an empty file. The embedded text layer varies by era and the earlier claim here was too broad: it is close to unreadable on the 1990s and 2005 scans, where you should render at 300 dpi with PyMuPDF and run ocrmac instead, but on the 2002-2009 Heralds it is GOOD and far better than OCR. Test the text layer before spending hours OCRing. This opens every scanned Herald and Talisman on TopSCHOLAR to plain scripts and removes the reason _topscholar-wanted.json existed.

topic: THE WAYBACK ROUTE, SECOND URL FORM
note: The cgi form web/2024id_/.../cgi/viewcontent.cgi?article=N&context=C works for most of TopSCHOLAR but the Internet Archive has no snapshot of some items: context=stu_org articles 1342-1379 404 on it. A second form reaches those: web/2024id_/https://digitalcommons.wku.edu/context/<collection>/article/<N>/type/native/viewcontent That is how the Phi Mu composites came in, at 3400x2500. Try the cgi form first and fall back to this one; between them TopSCHOLAR is effectively open to plain scripts. CORRECTION: Kappler and Lineweaver were Sigma Kappa, not Phi Mu. There is no Sigma Kappa composite on TopSCHOLAR, so that route is closed, not open.

topic: HERALD CAPTION INDEX 2010-2016, BUILT 4 SEPTEMBER 2026
note: The companion this archive was missing. ~/Desktop/SGA60 photo hunt/_herald-index-2010-2016/ now holds, for every digitised print Herald from 2010 to 2016 that the Internet Archive will serve, the full text of every page (herald_text*.jsonl) and one row per embedded photograph (photo_captions*.jsonl) carrying its xref, its native pixel size, its rectangle on the page, and the text immediately BELOW it, to its RIGHT and ABOVE it. That is over 27,000 photographs. Grep it before fetching anything for these years; it is the direct equivalent of _herald-index-2002-2009 and it is what turned up the Kat Johns vox-pop mugshot. The 'above' field is new and matters: the Herald sets a lot of its mugshot labels above the frame, not below. Note two shapes of false positive it will hand you: full-column advertisements whose neighbouring text is the story beside them, and sidebar boxes of names set as images.

topic: THE WAYBACK ROUTE HAS A CONCURRENCY CEILING
note: web.archive.org serves these PDFs at roughly 0.5 to 1 MB/s per connection and will accept about four connections from one address. A fifth gets 'Failed to connect to web.archive.org port 80' rather than an HTTP error, and a harvester that treats that as a missing snapshot will silently skip real issues. Run three or four workers, never more; give curl --connect-timeout 25 --speed-time 25 --speed-limit 20000; and on curl exit codes 7, 28, 35, 52 or 56 back off twenty seconds and retry the SAME url rather than falling through to the /context/.../type/native/viewcontent form, which costs another timeout. Never mark an issue done on a failed fetch. Sustained pulling for an hour or two visibly slows the whole thing down, so plan the run long rather than wide.

name: SGA's own election advertisements in the Herald
detail: SGA bought full pages in the Herald at election time and they are the best portrait source in the 2008-2010 window, because they are one name to one face with the name set in large type beside the photograph. topic: WAYBACK: PARALLEL RANGE REQUESTS BEAT A SINGLE STREAM BY TWO ORDERS OF MAGNITUDE
note: The 2016 Talisman is 755,645,090 bytes and a single curl was pulling it at about 30 KB/s after an hour of sustained use, which would have taken another hour. web.archive.org honours HTTP Range on these files. Ask for one byte with -r 0-0 -D - and the response carries content-range: bytes 0-0/755645090, which gives you the true size; then split the remainder into four ranges and fetch them in parallel with curl -r a-b. The last 111 MB came down in about two minutes, exact byte counts, and concatenating them onto the truncated file produced a PDF that opens cleanly. Use this for any Talisman; four ranges is within the concurrency ceiling.

topic: THE 2016 TALISMAN IS THE PORTRAIT BOOK FOR 2008-2016

topic: WAYBACK MECHANICS
note: About four concurrent connections is the ceiling; a fifth fails in a way that looks like a missing snapshot rather than a refused connection, so it is easy to misread as 'not archived'. Parallel HTTP Range requests beat a single stream by two orders of magnitude on the large Talismans: the last 111 MB of a 755 MB file came down in two minutes.

detail: Entered twice, as Amber Daniels (justice, 2014-15) and Amber Daniel (chief justice, 2015-16). One woman on one council in consecutive years is far likelier than two whose names differ by a single s, and years.json already notes that by the Senate meeting of 2 February 2016 'a justice named Amber Daniel had been elected chief justice'. Only the singular form has a WKU account handle on SGA's own pages, amber.daniel183, and only the singular form appears in either Talisman, as 'Daniel, Amber H.' in the 2016 Sigma Kappa roster and 'Daniel, Amber' in the 2015 equivalent. Not merged here because the archive's rule is to flag rather than fix, and because Carlene and Darlene Lodmell are the standing warning against merging on name similarity alone.

topic: HERALD PRINT CAPTION INDEX NOW REACHES 2019, BUILT 4 SEPTEMBER 2026
note: The 2010-2016 index has been extended three years. ~/Desktop/SGA60 photo hunt/_herald-index-2010-2016/ now also holds photo_captions_2017-2019.jsonl and photo_captions_2017-2019b.jsonl plus the matching herald_text files: 96 of the 99 digitised print Heralds of 2017, 2018 and 2019, 988 embedded photographs, each with its xref, native pixel size, rectangle and the text below, right of and above it. Combined with the same result from the 2010-2016 index and from the whole wkuherald.com media library, this is the hard evidence for the pattern earlier blocks suspected - the Herald quotes committee chairs and justices constantly and almost never photographs them.

name: Talisman magazines 2016-2020
detail: The Talisman stopped being a yearbook after the 2016 volume and became a twice-yearly magazine: dlsc_ua_records 8678 (2016 Identity), 8685 (2017 Well Being), 8686 (2017 Power), 8684 (2018 Grit), 8690 (2018 Movement), 8682 (2019 Paradise), 8683 (2019 Balance), 8681 (2020 Zeitgeist). topic: THE 2016 TALISMAN ALSO CARRIES GRADUATE STUDENTS AND A STAFF GRID - AND THREE OF THIS BLOCK'S FINDS CAME FROM THEM
note: The note above says do not skip the faculty and staff grid. Add the GRADUATE STUDENT grid, pp. 296-299, to that warning. Elicia Tillis, an SGA senator and Cultural and Diversity Affairs chair in 2014-15, and Omer Toqeer, a senator appointed in January 2016, are both in it and neither is anywhere else in the archive's reach. An officer who is invisible in the senior and underclassmen grids may simply have been a graduate student. Mechanics for the whole portrait section, verified: PDF page i carries printed folios 2i-2 on the left and 2i-1 on the right, except that PDF 130, 131, 150 and 151 are single pages. Seniors are three portraits to a row at 641x641 native; underclassmen and graduate students are four to a row at 510x510; the margin names sit in the OUTER margin, far left on a left page and far right on a right page, in one column grouped by row. Verify every claim by counting sexes down the row - it resolved every page worked on this run - and note two anchors that make it certain on the pages that have them: p. 285 row 5 opens with the name BIG RED against the mascot in costume, and p. 260 row 4 position 3 is Andrea Ambam, whose face the archive already publishes.

topic: TALISMAN MAGAZINES 2016-2020 ARE NOW ON DISK
note: All eight are at ~/Desktop/SGA60 photo hunt/_topscholar-pdfs/talisman-mag-*.pdf, about 450 MB, pulled through the Wayback route. They have no portrait grids and no index of people, and their staff and editorial-board pages carry no photographs at all, which closes an obvious-looking lead: Sophie Whorf was the magazine's marketing manager for two years, Tony Piedmonte and Dillon McCormick wrote for it for four, and none of them is pictured. What they DO have is captioned photo stories, and one of those gave the only face of Elias Thompson that exists anywhere - 2019 Balance, p. 52, whose caption is positional ('LEFT:'). Grep the text layer, it is clean.

name: John Winstead
detail: The withdrawal register refused the Herald's mugshot of its Synthesis columnist because nothing tied the columnist to student government. The Herald ties them in its news text, three times, which is why every caption sweep missed it: 'SGA senator John Winstead, who is also an opinion columnist for the Herald' (3 Dec 2015), 'John Winstead, who is also a columnist for the Herald' (29 Mar 2016), and 'John Winstead, SGA senator and Herald columnist' (29 Mar 2016). GENERAL LESSON, worth more than this one case: a do-not-use entry that turns on 'no caption says so' should be retested against ARTICLE TEXT before it is treated as final. Three of this block's four standing refusals fell to that test - Winstead, Brian Anderson (the SGA officer is a WKU Forensics Team member, said outright in two April 2017 letters) and Elias Thompson.

name: The Herald never photographs SGA committee chairs and justices, 2014-2020
detail: Earlier blocks suspected this; it is now measured. All 44 officers of the n1419 list and all 108 names of its officer and worklist files were run against four separate photograph indexes: the live wkuherald.com media library searched name by name (the authoritative one, not a cache), data/herald-photos.json with 21,304 captions from 2010 to 2026, the print caption index for 2010-2016 with 23,252 photographs, and the new print caption index for 2017-2019 with 988. Of the 44 officers, five appear in a Herald caption and four of those five frames are refused. Yet the same people are quoted constantly: Mark Clark in 21 articles, Ian Hamilton in 15, Cassidy Townsend and Josh Knight in 14 each, William Hurst in 11, Matt Barr in 11, Josh Zaczek and Ryan Richardson in 10 each. The paper covers SGA as votes and quotations and photographs almost nobody but the president and the election-night winners. A later block should not spend a run re-proving this; go to the yearbooks, to SGA's own headshot directories, and to the university photograph directory instead.

topic: img_facstaff RETURNS 200 FOR A PHOTO THAT DOES NOT EXIST
note: wku.edu/img_facstaff/<handle>.jpg answers HTTP 200 with an identical WKU-logo placeholder when the person has no photograph: md5 819cd6b1bf686b3881d1434c635e3a1f, exactly 39,409 bytes. A status-code check will happily file the same logo as three different people. Always hash the body. Of 101 handles tested, 79 were the placeholder, including all 26 recoverable handles for the 2014-19 officers, so that route is exhausted for that cohort.

topic: RETEST A REFUSAL AGAINST ARTICLE TEXT, NOT JUST CAPTIONS
note: Three of the four standing refusals on 2014-19 fell to one test. Each rested on the reasoning that no caption ties the person to SGA — but the Herald states the tie in ARTICLE TEXT and caption sweeps never see it. John Winstead's columnist mugshot was refused for exactly that reason, and the paper wrote 'SGA senator John Winstead, who is also an opinion columnist for the Herald' three separate times. Before accepting a 'no caption says so' refusal, search the body text of the issues around it.

topic: SGA'S OWN 2003-04 WEBSITE SURVIVES, ITS PHOTOGRAPHS DO NOT
note: The Wayback Machine holds SGA's own j_profiles.html and l_profiles.html from 2003-04, which carry a portrait per member with the name in the IMG ALT and a Name: field beside it — Gretchen Light, Kristin Hartley and Tim Howard among them. **The image files were never archived**: all thirteen PNGs 404. The HTML survives and the pictures do not. Recorded because if a WKU server backup ever surfaces, this is the exact file list to ask for, and because it otherwise reads as a promising lead every time somebody finds it.

topic: SPIRIT MASTERS SCRAPBOARDS PAIR BY COLUMN, PROVABLY
note: The Spirit Masters scrapbook boards list names beside a block of portraits, which looks like an unprovable grid. It is not: on two separate pages the only man named is also the only man pictured, each in his own column, which fixes the column pairing. Two colour studio portraits at 1200x1700 came out of the 2007-08 board that way, far better than any newsprint frame. Nine scrapbooks are inventoried by year.

topic: READING FLAT-IMAGE SCANS, 2002-2006
note: Those years scan as flat images and defeat every text index. Method that works: search the ocrmac output for text runs that are EXACTLY a target's name, rank them by type height, then tell a caption from a list by counting same-height neighbours. A caption stands alone in its size; a roster line has siblings. Two frames came out that nothing else could see. The Spirit Master adverts yield to the same idea: the advert's repeating border is itself indexed, so a box-union renders the whole advert in one step rather than hunting it by eye.
